purpose: Make incident-repair regression fixtures independent of the repository's live lifecycle so the exact terminal closure can be proven without tests inheriting terminal state as their synthetic ACTIVE repair fixture.

lineage.outcome: Incident-repair regression proof remains valid when the real repository transitions from ACTIVE repair to terminal closure, without weakening closure semantics or mutating product code.

why_now: After #249 and #259 merged and were post-merge verified, three independent exact terminal-closure candidates (#260, #261 and #262) passed trusted structural admission but failed the same Linux/macOS full-regression seam. The failures show tests cloning live terminal active_receipt/current_state and then accidentally exercising closure validation instead of their intended synthetic ACTIVE governance or MERGED_PRODUCT repair cases; the duplicate-ID test also assumes exactly one pre-existing #206 event. The closure contract itself must stay strict, so the fixtures must become lifecycle-independent before closure is rebuilt.

implementation_contract.test_isolation: Synthetic incident-repair tests explicitly construct the ACTIVE state and incident history they require rather than inheriting current repository lifecycle or current event count.
implementation_contract.history_relative: Duplicate-ID event-history assertions compare against the number of matching rows present before the synthetic append, so legitimate durable history growth does not invalidate the test.
implementation_contract.current_incident_fixture: Synthetic repair tests use one explicit current OPEN #206 fixture instead of accidentally inheriting later repair-completion events.
implementation_contract.noninterference: No production checker, product code, semantic scope, incident truth, closure contract, or authority boundary changes in this continuation.

completion_proof: the exact #260/#261/#262 regression signatures are eliminated without changing production closure semantics
governance and merged-product exact-path tests exercise explicit ACTIVE fixtures even when repository root is terminal
closure lifecycle tests begin from an explicit ACTIVE synthetic repair and remain valid after real closure
incident event-history duplicate-ID test asserts one additional event relative to initial durable history
candidate diff is exactly the ACTIVE receipt plus the three governance test files
fresh exact-head Linux, Windows and macOS governance, full regression and consumer smoke pass before integration
substantive exact-head review is terminal before merge
non_scope: closing the #247/#248 ACTIVE repair in this candidate
next_selection_rule: After this exact fixture-isolation continuation is merged and post-merge verified, rebuild exactly one three-file INCIDENT_REPAIR_CLOSURE from fresh main, prove/review/merge/post-merge verify it, then globally select the next bounded #206 repair.
